newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAL says prefers separate alliances.
newsitem.headline: JAL says prefers separate alliances.

text.p: Japan Airlines (JAL) said on Thursday that it prefers separate alliances for different regions rather than participating in global alliances like the Star Alliance.
"Having separate networks with suitable partners in each region of the world is enough to serve our customers' needs," JAL president Akira Kondo told a new conference.
He said that airlines around the world were experimenting with different and new types of alliances but that in his opinion separate networks were still more advantageous.
He did not go into further detail.

In May, a group of major airlines, including Deutsche Lufthansa AG and United Airlines formally branded an existing partnership under the name Star Alliance, aiming to create a global image for the alliance.
Kondo said that JAL already has separate alliances with American Airlines, Thai Airways and Air France.
He added that JAL and American Airlines were likely to code-share when and if the United States and Japan reach a new interim agreement in their civil aviation talks.
"We will code-share with American Airlines once the rules are set in the aviation talks," he said.
Tokyo and Washington have agreed to strike an interim aviation accord by the end of September. Talks to work on the agreement will held in Tokyo from August 4 to 6.
